fact: The METISS consortium states that the 3,200 km METISS submarine cable, linking Mauritius, Réunion and Madagascar to a landing near Durban in South Africa, entered service on 5 March 2021, its first links to Africa already used by the consortium operators' customers.

Liquid Dataport (Cassava Technologies) announced on 16 May 2023 that it had launched the first terrestrial-only fibre route from Mombasa in Kenya to Johannesburg, through Uganda, Rwanda, the DRC, Zambia and Zimbabwe, giving carriers, enterprises and hyperscalers direct connectivity to data centres in Johannesburg and Nairobi.

fact: Broadband Infraco's chief executive said in July 2019 that the state wholesaler's network provides connectivity to all six neighbouring countries, Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Swaziland and Lesotho, and that its Beitbridge point of presence carries Zimbabwe's broadband traffic to Johannesburg data centres.

Google stated on 23 May 2024 that the terrestrial path of its Umoja fibre route, from Kenya through Uganda, Rwanda, the DRC, Zambia and Zimbabwe to South Africa, had been built with Liquid Intelligent Technologies, with the Indian Ocean crossing to Australia still to come.
